issues.issue: Should the Court decide the Minister's new argument that the issues can be re-argued before the ID, so the appeal is premature?
issues.applicant_position: Minister argued late that the appeal should not be decided because the issues can be re-argued at the ID; did not press it at hearing.
issues.respondent_position: Tran says the new argument is surprising, since the Minister sought an expedited hearing, and that he already incurred legal costs.
issues.result_quote: after careful consideration, I have concluded that it would be inappropriate to do so in this somewhat exceptional case

issues.issue: Is the Minister's interpretation of s.36(1)(a) (maximum punishment assessed objectively, under the law in force when admissibility is decided) reasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Minister says the maximum punishment is assessed objectively under the law in force at admissibility, which fits the statute's text and purpose.
issues.respondent_position: Tran says the maximum must be assessed for him personally under Charter s.11(g) and (i) (7 years); otherwise the result is retrospective and absurd.
issues.result_quote: I cannot conclude that the interpretation adopted by the Minister’s delegate is unreasonable

issues.issue: Is a conditional sentence a 'term of imprisonment' under s.36(1)(a)?
issues.applicant_position: Minister says conditional sentences are generally imprisonment under the Criminal Code, and the wording and history of s.64 support including them.
issues.respondent_position: Tran says the words mean only carceral jail time, given Proulx, the 2007 and 2012 limits on conditional sentences, and its serious-criminality purpose.
issues.result_quote: may reasonably be construed as a term of imprisonment under paragraph 36(1)(a) of the IRPA

issues.issue: Was the delegate's decision to refer Tran to an admissibility hearing reasonable, given its reliance on arrests and unproven charges?
issues.applicant_position: Minister says the referral was reasonable: the officer knew arrests are not convictions and could weigh them for credibility and rehabilitation.
issues.respondent_position: Tran says the delegate treated arrests and unproven charges as proof of past criminal conduct, so the decision is unreasonable.
issues.result_quote: The decision to refer Mr. Tran to the ID was within the range of outcomes defensible on the law and the facts.
